newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER SHOWCASE-FEYENOORD-PSV IN POSSIBLE TITLE-DECIDER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-FEYENOORD-PSV IN POSSIBLE TITLE-DECIDER.

text.p: Sunday's clash between Feyenoord Rotterdam and PSV Eindhoven could go a long way towards deciding the Dutch league championship -- with Ajax, 26 times champions and four-times European Cup winners, for once only among the also-rans.
PSV and Feyenoord, who have each won the Dutch title 13 times, are first and second in the standings with PSV three points ahead. Ajax are down in fifth another 15 points away.
In recent times, PSV have fared better in the league, winning the title four times in the last 10 years, compared with Feyenoord's single success in 1993.

This season, PSV have again played the better football, particularly in big games. Both sides have crumbled in Europe, but PSV have beaten Ajax at home, while Feyenoord lost 3-0 to their arch-rivals last month.
And in an extraordinary result earlier in the season, PSV demolished the Rotterdammers with a record 7-2 thrashing.
Recent history in Rotterdam however favours Feyenoord, who have not lost at home to PSV in 10 years.
Feyenoord's home form is their traditional strength. Their impressive 50,000 capacity stadium is generally full of noisy, passionate fans - something PSV have never had.
Some observers see Sunday's match as a challenge between Feyenoord's honest grafters and the aristocratic, bought-in talents of PSV.

PSV is sometimes represented as a soulless, clean-cut businesslike club - an image that results largely from its long association with electronics giant Philips. The team's initials stand for Philips Sport Vereniging (club).
Few neutrals regard PSV with a great deal of fondness. This year's rising stars, third-placed Twente Enschede are popular underdogs, something PSV can never be.
Indeed many Ajax fans would prefer traditional rival Feyenoord won the championship rather than PSV. Feyenoord fans share a similar respect for Ajax and a disdain for PSV.
"We are teams which play from the heart. PSV do not," said one Ajax fan.
The match lacks the passion of the Dutch "classic" Ajax-Feyenoord, but is also a safer occasion.
A rising hooligan trend in recent months has caused Rotterdam's worried mayor to move from the evening to an afternoon kick-off.
Police will hope nothing happens on the pitch to incite violence in the stands - unlike a bizarre incident when the teams met in the late 1970s.
On that occasion Bertus Quaars of PSV was sent off for head-butting a linesman. It later transpired the linesman had butted Quaars.
